mfg1-surface-lesson-054.title: Identify steels and nonferrous metals using material designations
mfg1-surface-lesson-054.objective:
Explain the classification of iron-based and nonferrous metals.
Read density, melting-point and conductivity tables with their conditions.
mfg1-surface-lesson-054.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on classification, 8 on property tables and 7 explaining a material-check example. Write the limits of representative values in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-054.summary:
Separate classification, composition, properties and certificates.
Do not decide process changes from representative values alone.
safety: Do not identify unknown materials by putting them into chemicals.
Do not infer lifting or heating permission from a property table.

paragraphs.title: Separate main constituents from alloying elements
paragraphs.text: Study iron-based materials as materials mainly containing iron, with carbon and other elements. Steel, cast iron and different alloys vary in composition, workability and strength. Nonferrous metals are metals other than iron and steel, including copper, aluminium, zinc and nickel. Nonferrous does not mean identical magnetism or corrosion behavior.

paragraphs.title: Read the conditions of property tables
paragraphs.text: For equal volumes, greater density means greater mass. Density alone, however, cannot establish strength or material identity. Compare low melting point, high conductivity, corrosion resistance and workability separately according to purpose. Do not apply representative values to all alloys without qualification.

paragraphs.title: Connect alloys to surface treatment
paragraphs.text: Aluminium alloys such as duralumin, die-casting materials such as ADC 12 and zinc alloys differ in composition and production. A material change also affects pretreatment and adhesion, so compare drawings, material designations and lot certificates.

paragraphs.title: Similar weight does not identify a material
paragraphs.text: Two samples with similar masses are not necessarily the same metal or alloy. Check measurement error, cavities, shape and quantity too. Identify unknown-material items and send them for the responsible person's confirmation.

terms.meaning: The material category including steel and cast iron, mainly based on iron.
The category of metals other than iron and steel.
A standard or drawing designation used to identify a material.
A reference value under particular comparison conditions.

mfg1-surface-lesson-055.title: Separate adhesion, hardness and solder-wettability tests
mfg1-surface-lesson-055.objective:
Match the property being investigated to the test method.
Check destructive effects and sample management.
mfg1-surface-lesson-055.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on three properties, 8 on methods and samples and 7 organizing the contact-part example. Write how to identify tested items in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-055.summary:
Distinguish test objectives and applied effects.
Passing appearance checks does not replace other performance tests.
safety: Do not independently perform tests using heat or chemicals.
Do not return bent or tested items to unused stock.

paragraphs.title: Adhesion concerns the interface
paragraphs.text: Adhesion tests investigate how firmly a coating attaches to its substrate. Tape peeling, bending, filing and thermal shock apply different effects and do not necessarily produce identical results. Check the specified method, sample and decision criteria.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish hardness and solder wettability
paragraphs.text: Hardness tests investigate resistance to indentation and related effects. Methods include micro-Vickers, Rockwell and Brinell. The responsible person selects a method suited to load, surface condition and film thickness. Solder wettability evaluates how solder spreads over a surface and similar behavior; hardness or color cannot substitute for it.

paragraphs.title: Do not mix samples back with products
paragraphs.text: Bending, scratching, heating or chemical action during a test may prevent return to the original shipping condition. Follow sampling plans and identification requirements. Do not mix tested items with unused conforming items. Judge method suitability and product conformity using the specified criteria.

paragraphs.title: Check additional specification requirements
paragraphs.text: Even if a contact component passes color and thickness checks, do not omit specified solder-wettability confirmation when joining performance is required. Operators must not improvise heating conditions; ask quality personnel about the sample and method.

terms.meaning: The property of a coating adhering to its substrate.
An index of resistance to indentation and related effects.
The property of solder wetting and spreading over a surface.
A test evaluating a sample by changing or damaging it.

mfg1-surface-lesson-056.title: Separate pollution categories and sources of chemical information
mfg1-surface-lesson-056.objective:
Organize environmental effects beyond water and air.
Do not confuse the purposes of RoHS and REACH.
mfg1-surface-lesson-056.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on seven impacts, 8 on the two systems and 7 organizing a customer inquiry. Write the distinction from workplace emissions in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-056.summary:
Separate environmental pathways from product substances.
Check current requirements rather than inferring compliance from a system's name.
safety: Do not declare legal or customer-specification compliance from the learning material alone.
Do not investigate by mixing or discharging unknown liquids.

paragraphs.title: Consider multiple impact pathways
paragraphs.text: Distinguish water, air and soil pollution, noise, vibration, ground subsidence and offensive odors. Clear wastewater or weak odor does not establish that the whole factory has no impact. Record floor leaks and waste movements too, and consider prevention and reduction.

paragraphs.title: Product substances differ from workplace emissions
paragraphs.text: RoHS is an EU system restricting certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment. It is not the same as workplace wastewater control values. The responsible person checks current requirements, including covered products, materials and exemptions. Do not declare compliance from a chemical name alone.

paragraphs.title: Do not reduce REACH to registration
paragraphs.text: REACH is an EU system covering registration, evaluation, authorization and restriction of chemicals. Communication and use conditions also apply according to roles. It does not mean registering all product information permits every use. Check current information for specific obligations based on substance, quantity and supply-chain role.

paragraphs.title: Compare information when changes occur
paragraphs.text: If a customer asks about contained substances, organize the item number, edition, composition information, supplier evidence and applicable conditions for the responsible person. Do not assume the SDS alone satisfies all requirements; check necessary documents and analyses. Learning material does not replace specific legal compliance decisions.

terms.meaning: Pollution and similar effects causing harm to health or the living environment.
A substance contained in a product or material.
An EU system restricting certain hazardous substances in electrical and electronic equipment.
An EU system involving chemical registration, evaluation, authorization and restriction.

mfg1-surface-lesson-057.title: Compare surface treatments by film formation and purpose
mfg1-surface-lesson-057.objective:
Distinguish adding a coating from changing a surface.
Do not choose a method solely from representative thickness.
mfg1-surface-lesson-057.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 comparing four methods, 8 on substrates and thickness tables and 7 comparing changed applications. Write the distinction between specifications and guides in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-057.summary:
Classify by formation mechanism and substrate.
A comparison-table guide is different from a product specification.
safety: Do not decide actual equipment conditions from method names or guide thicknesses.
Obtain material, process and quality approvals for treatment changes.

paragraphs.title: Separate formation methods and functions
paragraphs.text: Plating forms metal coatings; anodizing oxidizes the substrate surface; chemical conversion forms compound films through reactions; painting uses resin and other paints. Their formation mechanisms differ. Thermal spraying, etching, polishing, quenching and nitriding also change surfaces; do not call them all plating.

paragraphs.title: Check substrates and applications
paragraphs.text: Methods also exist for applying metal coatings to resins and other nonmetals, but appropriate pretreatment and material conditions are necessary. Anodizing does not work on every metal under identical conditions. Compare material names, underlayers, outermost layers, and electrical and thermal conditions.

paragraphs.title: Comparison ranges are not specifications
paragraphs.text: Textbook thickness ranges and applications are guides for comparing methods. Do not directly turn general plating, anodizing, conversion or paint thicknesses into acceptance limits or equipment settings for individual products. Link requirements for appearance, corrosion, wear, joining and electrical properties through to inspection.

paragraphs.title: Compare a changed application
paragraphs.text: If a part changes from decorative use to an electrical contact, choosing the same color is insufficient. Check conduction and contact, layer structure, wear and corrosion requirements with the responsible person, then choose an approved process.

terms.meaning: Creating a layer on a surface for a desired purpose.
A method that creates a coating by heating and spraying material or similar means.
Removing or machining a surface by chemical or other methods.
A representative example of a method's use.

mfg1-surface-lesson-058.title: Check substrate-specific pretreatment and underlayer compatibility
mfg1-surface-lesson-058.objective:
Separate conditions for steel, stainless steel, copper and light metals.
Do not transfer named underlayer treatments without conditions.
mfg1-surface-lesson-058.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on five materials, 8 on underlayer roles and 7 drafting a change inquiry. Explain control of unconfirmed items in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-058.summary:
A substrate change requires pretreatment and inspection checks.
Distinguish thin underlayer and main-coating roles.
safety: Do not put a material into acid to test its reaction.
Do not change underlayer solutions or treatment order without authorization.

paragraphs.title: A metal name alone does not determine the process
paragraphs.text: Steel, stainless steel, copper alloys, aluminium alloys and magnesium alloys have different surfaces and chemical properties. Even if general applications use nickel or chromium, identical pretreatment may not apply. Check item number, material certificate, oxidation or contamination and required quality.

paragraphs.title: Separate underlayers from the main coating
paragraphs.text: A thin strike underlayer or pretreatment such as zincating relates to adhesion of the later coating. Its role differs from thickening the main coating. Do not invent chemical recipes or electrical conditions from a name; use the process approved for the target material.

paragraphs.title: Light metals and nonconductive substrates
paragraphs.text: For aluminium and similar materials, check the relationship between oxide film and pretreatment. Do not unconditionally transfer a similarly named process to magnesium or another material. Plating resins and other nonconductive substrates also requires checks of pretreatment, catalysts, conductive preparation and material compatibility.

paragraphs.title: Hold a material change
paragraphs.text: If drawing material changes but the process sheet still specifies the old material, past success with the old sheet is insufficient. Ask about the change, underlayer and main coating, pretreatment and inspection requirements. Identify the affected items as awaiting confirmation.

terms.meaning: A metal layer applied before the main coating.
A thin underlayer plating used for adhesion or related purposes.
Treatment providing an electrical path needed for the next process.
A treatment matching the target material and its condition.

mfg1-surface-lesson-059.title: Read hot-dip plating types and alloy layers
mfg1-surface-lesson-059.objective:
Distinguish zinc-, aluminium- and tin-based applications.
Check the relationship between alloy layers and dimensions.
mfg1-surface-lesson-059.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on types, 8 on alloy layers and dimensions and 7 comparing process sheets. Separate guide conditions from specifications in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-059.summary:
Match type, substrate, alloy layer and required dimensions.
Even with immersion, do not transfer another bath's conditions.
safety: Do not put wet items or items with unknown internal liquid residues into molten baths.
Do not independently change bath metals or cooling conditions.

paragraphs.title: Identify the molten bath metal
paragraphs.text: Hot-dip methods include zinc, zinc-aluminium, aluminium and tin systems. Uses include steel corrosion protection, construction materials, heat-resistant applications and containers, according to required properties. Similar bath names do not mean identical composition or processes.

paragraphs.title: Layers can also form at the interface
paragraphs.text: Some substrate and molten-metal combinations form an alloy layer at the interface. Consider that layer, thickness, shape and dimensional requirements as well as the outer surface. Cooling conditions also matter; do not independently set temperatures or times from a principles explanation.

paragraphs.title: Compare corrosion protection and service conditions
paragraphs.text: Zinc systems provide sacrificial protection, but thicker does not improve every property. Check threads, fits, edges and the service environment. A general statement that tin is harmless does not guarantee every bath, additive or food-contact application.

paragraphs.title: Compare types
paragraphs.text: If zinc-based and aluminium-based process sheets are side by side, the shared immersion method does not make them interchangeable. Check substrate, process number, required performance and dimensions before sending items to the designated process.

terms.meaning: A layer at an interface or elsewhere formed through different metal constituents.
A category of materials or treatments mainly containing zinc.
Parts fitting together.
The boundary between two materials or layers.

mfg1-surface-lesson-060.title: Distinguish pinholes, pits and runs by their shape
mfg1-surface-lesson-060.objective:
Use cross-section concepts to separate holes and uncoated areas.
Do not infer causes or acceptance from appearance names alone.
mfg1-surface-lesson-060.activity: Spend 4 minutes on terms, 8 on three cross-sections, 8 on runs and decisions and 7 preparing a projection report. Separate causal hypotheses and appearance names in 3 minutes.
mfg1-surface-lesson-060.summary:
Separate hole depth, coating separation and excess attachment.
A name alone does not determine cause, acceptance or reprocessing.
safety: Do not grind, crush or chemically treat defects without authorization.
Follow the responsible person's sample plan for sectioning.

paragraphs.title: How far does the hole reach?
paragraphs.text: In this electroplating category, a pinhole is a small hole through the coating to the substrate; a pit is a depression that does not reach the substrate. A visible dot alone cannot establish depth; use the specified observation and inspection method. Both can affect quality, so shallow does not mean unconditional acceptance.

paragraphs.title: Distinguish blisters and unplated areas
paragraphs.text: A blister is a raised coating separated from the substrate. An unplated area lacks coating where it is required. Preserve location, extent, observation conditions, pretreatment and contact history. Recording every similar appearance as a pinhole makes investigation difficult.

paragraphs.title: Hot-dip runs
paragraphs.text: Study a run as excess molten metal attached at an edge or similar location. Temperature, flow, withdrawal and shape can contribute, but appearance alone does not identify one cause. Dimensions, safe handling and quality requirements also matter. A general textbook explanation does not authorize leaving it or grinding it off.

paragraphs.title: Record separately from conforming items
paragraphs.text: If you find an edge projection, preserve its location diagram, dimensions and lot, identify it separately from conforming items and consult. Even a suspected pinhole must not be enlarged with a needle or tested with chemicals; send it for approved inspection.

terms.meaning: In this category, a small hole through the coating to the substrate.
In this category, a coating depression not reaching the substrate.
Excess hot-dip metal attached at edges or similar locations.
The structure considered as a surface cut through an object.
